name: XDK Direct3D 8 LTCG whose fence wait spins on the 0x0310 latch (D3D8LTCG, any build)
_why: XBA_D3D_DMA_WALK=1 (RECOMP_PB_WALK=dma unless set): D3D8LTCG's fence wait (BlockOnTime and its far-behind
probe sub_0026CBA0 in Black) reads DMA_GET and the 0x0310 latch (PGRAPH 0x400B10), which only the DMA walk keeps
honest; under the segment scan it can spin for good on the latch (Black froze at the menu under host load), and
software method 5 is never delivered. With the walk on, profiles/xdk/d3d8/d3d8.c adopts the fence event once it
has found the device at run time, so BlockOnTime sleeps until method 5 sets it.
Picked by what the title's D3D does, not by its build (XBA-105): tools.xbe_ident's d3d_latch_wait probe finds the
latch loop (mov r32, [reg + 0x400B10] then test/and with the fence bits 0x7C) in the executable sections. Before,
builds [5849, 5849] only: other D3D8LTCG builds got no walk, silently. Plain D3D8 stays out (Fable, KOTOR run on
the segment scan, K-7); the triage's probe column shows which D3D8 titles carry the loop too.
No hooks: the D3D8 layer's code does the work. Seen on: Black 45410083, Burnout 3 4541005B (XDK 5849).
